title: Prompted introspection: does telling a model how steering works increase its self-detection?

original_idea.body: Inject concept vectors under neutral vs introspection-primer prompts, measure self-report accuracy, and compare to an internal probe.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Self-report vs internal-probe gap bears on honesty/monitoring, but the chain to catastrophic-risk reduction is indirect.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Inject vectors under two prompt conditions + compare verbal report to probe; guided, novice + mentor feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable but compares two conditions plus a probe baseline.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public model, no internal access; honesty/introspection monitoring is externally doable, lab-deprioritized.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + cheap probe on a small model; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Introspection-prompt boost is published; measuring it on small open models + probe comparison is partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The introspection-prompt boost is published; quantifying it on small models versus an internal probe is a partly-open extension.
